item.title: Bella Thorne says Hollywood treated her like a kid on screen and an adult off camera
item.description: Bella Thorne opens up about the moment she turned 18 and finally felt free after years of navigating Hollywood's impossible child star expectations.
item.content:encoded:
Bella Thorne's life as a child star came with a harsh reality: Hollywood expected her to be a kid on screen and an adult everywhere else.

Thorne began working in entertainment as a child, appearing as a model before taking on television roles in shows including HBO’s "Big Love." Her major breakthrough arrived in 2010 when she was cast as CeCe Jones opposite Zendaya’s Rocky Blue in Disney Channel’s "Shake It Up."

"You're ... spending all of your hours a day on set with adults, you know, that is – it's like such a different, the brain's like how do I–" Thorne explained during an appearance on "Call Her Daddy."

GOLDIE HAWN SOUNDS THE ALARM ON CHILDHOOD CELEBRITY CULTURE: 'ALL I CAN SAY IS IT'S A NIGHTMARE'

"And I'm expected to be this child, but I'm also working like hours like an adult and being in adult conversations," she added. "And when I f--k up it's my bad, not like a child – It's my bad. Like you're an adult, it's your bad."

But navigating those adult expectations while growing up in the public eye didn't come easily for Thorne.

"Well, I think people can see how I've managed it publicly," she told host Alexandra Cooper. "They can see it, they've got photos of it. Oh, they got all the photos. Oh, wow. I don't know that I ever handled it or balanced it out correctly."

"I don't think that I ever had that mental clarity," Thorne acknowledged. "I've worked a lot on the more recent side. I got to a point where I just needed to kind of change things in my life and get better at – I was working so much and yet was leaving very little time for the things that I really, really cared about."

FORMER DISNEY STAR MAITLAND WARD SAYS YOUNG ACTORS WERE TREATED LIKE A 'PRODUCT' IN HOLLYWOOD FACTORY

Thorne said she spent the past two years working to prioritize her mental health, a shift that became especially important after "Color Your Hurt" left her feeling emotionally drained. The now 28-year-old actress revealed she finally gave herself "some space to breathe" along with grace.

"I don't think I ever did that when I was younger," she said.

While Thorne struggled to give herself that same grace as a child star, she recalled feeling a dramatic shift when she turned 18.

"...I was like, 'I'm free,'" the "Midnight Sun" star recalled.

"Like I'm literally free. Like I'm walking into this house and no one's asking me when I'm like, when I'm gonna be there, when this time or when I'm gonna leave. It ... was such a weird – and you don't know what's weird until someone else tells you it's weird."

Thorne also spoke candidly about being compared to her fellow Disney Channel stars, including Selena Gomez, Miley Cyrus and Demi Lovato.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"I didn't so much hang out with people from the network," Thorne recalled. "I hung out with Zendaya, we hung out ... 'Shake It Up' was in a different time when Miley and Selena and Demi and those shows – They were all, I think 16, 17 when we were starting. So the eras are so different, and yet they intersect."

She said people questioned whether she would become Disney's next "bad girl," something she struggled to comprehend at such a young age.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"And I remember when I was 12, people asking me if I was gonna be – comparing us all, all the Disney girls and with Miley and Selena and this new era – and asking which was gonna be the next bad girl," Thorne claimed. "And, 'Are you gonna be like Lindsay Lohan?' And like all these things at 12, 13 – you're just, your brain is like trying so hard. 'Like am I gonna be like what? Like what? What is the question?' Like, oh my God."

Thorne later moved beyond her Disney image with a steady mix of film and television roles.

Thorne has also made a bigger push behind the camera. In August 2026, she signed on to write, direct and star in "Spring Breakers 2," following her feature directorial debut, "Color Your Hurt."

item.title: Trump's Justice Department sues New York, other blue states over tuition for illegal immigrants
item.description: Trump's DOJ filed lawsuits against New York, Connecticut, and Vermont over laws it claims provide in-state tuition and financial assistance to illegal immigrants.
item.content:encoded:
The Department of Justice under the Trump administration announced Monday that it plans to file lawsuits against New York, Connecticut and Vermont over laws that it claims provide in-state tuition and other financial incentives to illegal immigrants.

"These laws unconstitutionally discriminate against U.S. citizens who are not afforded the same reduced tuition rates or scholarships, create incentives for illegal immigration, and reward illegal aliens with benefits that U.S. citizens are not eligible for, all in direct conflict with federal law," a statement from the department read.

According to the legal complaints, the Department of Justice is seeking to enjoin enforcement of laws that provide financial assistance to illegal immigrants or provide tuition rates to any immigrants "who maintain in-state residency, regardless of whether they are lawfully present."

NEBRASKA ENDS IN-STATE TUITION BENEFITS FOR ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS UNDER DOJ DEAL

"This is a simple matter of federal law: colleges cannot provide benefits to illegal aliens that they do not provide to U.S. citizens," Assistant Attorney General Brett A. Shumate of the Justice Department’s Civil Division said in a press release. "This Department of Justice will not tolerate American students being treated like second-class citizens in their own country."

In a comment to Fox News Digital, the Department of Justice expressed confidence in its latest lawsuits, boasting legal wins in five other states with similar complaints.

"Under the leadership of Attorney General Todd Blanche, the Department’s efforts have already delivered wins for the American people, as five similar lawsuits in Texas, Kentucky, Oklahoma, Nebraska and Illinois have resulted favorable orders permanently enjoining and declaring unconstitutional analogous laws that gave reduced tuition to illegal aliens, including an order from the Fifth Circuit," the statement read.

OVER 100 CALIFORNIA COLLEGES ACCUSED OF DISCRIMINATING AGAINST US-BORN STUDENTS IN NEW DOJ COMPLAINT

Connecticut Attorney General William Tong pushed back on the lawsuit against his state in a comment to Fox News Digital on Tuesday.

"Note to Trump — stay out of Connecticut. How we run our schools and teach our kids is none of your business, and you have no authority to force the sovereign state of Connecticut to deny our kids a future," Tong said. "I fought for this bill as a legislator when it passed in 2011, and I’ll fight to defend Connecticut families now from this cruel attack. Connecticut offers in-state tuition and financial aid to all eligible Connecticut students because all kids deserve the opportunity to learn, to advance, and to achieve their dreams. Donald Trump doesn’t run UConn or any of our state colleges, and we’re not about to let him start."

FLORIDA BOARD VOTES TO BAN ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS FROM PUBLIC COLLEGE ADMISSIONS

Fox News Digital also reached out to New York and Vermont's attorneys general for comment on the developing lawsuits.

As of Monday, the Department of Justice has filed 17 lawsuits targeting laws that the Trump administration has claimed provide reduced tuition for illegal immigrants. The other states sued included Minnesota, Virginia, California, New Jersey, Kansas, Massachusetts, Rhode Island, Maryland and Colorado.

Last month, a federal judge provided a win for the Trump administration's Justice Department after ruling that Illinois' in-state tuition policies, the RISE Act and the Illinois DREAM Act, were "unconstitutional and invalid." The department originally sued Illinois in September 2025.

item.title: Trump directs CMS Administrator Mehmet Oz to end Medicaid gender transition funding for minors
item.description: Trump instructed CMS to end Medicaid funding for gender transition procedures, calling the surgeries "barbaric" in a Truth Social post.
item.content:encoded:
The Trump administration will no longer fund gender transition surgeries using Medicaid, President Don ald Trump said Tuesday. 

In a Truth Social post, Trump said he ordered Dr. Mehmet Oz, administrator of the US Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, to stop using the joint federal and state public health insurance program to fund such procedures. 

"We are not going to pay for our innocent children to undergo these barbaric surgeries and practices, which result in unthinkable and irreversible harm to their young bodies," Trump wrote.

item.title: A combination of bad coaching hires and subpar quarterback play is the culprit for SEC's recent swoon
item.description: SEC football hasn't won a national championship in three years despite adding Oklahoma and Texas, and coaching hires may be the biggest reason why.
item.content:encoded:
It has been a hotly debated topic in college football circles as to whether the SEC's reign of dominance has ended after a nearly 20-year run, and while I'm not here to bury the league just yet, it's hard to argue they've taken a step back.

From 2006 to 2023, an SEC team won a staggering 13 of a possible 17 national championships during the era of both the BCS and College Football Playoff.

However, the once-dominant Southeastern Conference hasn't won a championship in three years despite adding two traditional powers to its ranks (Oklahoma and Texas) and hasn't even reached the title game since Georgia won it all in January 2023.

PERCEPTION IS REALITY, AND THE SEC NEEDS TO START WINNING AGAIN BEFORE IT CONTINUES TO PUFF OUT ITS CHEST

Many people like to point to the advents of NIL and the transfer portal as the boogie men responsible for the SEC's downfall, but to me, it's a far more nuanced conversation than just saying "paying players is legal now, therefore the SEC sucks."

While there may not be a single issue that is easily identifiable, I can think of two reasons as to why the SEC has experienced its recent CFP swoon.

First, and perhaps most importantly, the coaching hires at several top-flight SEC programs have left much to be desired.

Some coaching changes were flat out downgrades from their predecessors while others, while not necessarily poor coaches in their own right, were terrible fits and never should have been considered in the first place.

Let's start with the two tentpole programs of the conference since the league went to a championship game format, Alabama and Florida.

Since the SEC expanded to 12 teams in 1992 and implemented the SEC Championship Game, both the Tide and Gators are first and second in league titles, with 11 and seven, respectively.

When the conference was in its early stages of ascending to dominance in the late 2000s, two of the greatest coaches of their era called Tuscaloosa and Gainesville home.

Nick Saban won six national championships while coaching the Crimson Tide, but when he called it quits in 2024, Alabama needed to find someone to fill his shoes.

Enter Kalen DeBoer.

DID ALABAMA DOOM THEMSELVES TO MEDIOCRITY WITH KALEN DEBOER EXTENSION?

Now, DeBoer isn't a bad coach, per se, but he isn't Saban, and Bama has failed to live up to its legendary status from the decade prior since he arrived.

For the Gators, it's been way worse since Urban Meyer left.

A program like Florida, with all its resources and in-state talent available, should never bottom out like it did in 2025, but the crazy thing is they've experienced three separate four-win seasons since the legendary coach Meyer walked out the door in 2010.

A run of subpar coaching hires culminated in the Billy Napier tenure, who was, by every metric, the worst coach in Gator football history since World War II.

His arrival coincided with the steady decline of the SEC starting with the 2023 season, and although Florida wasn't a perennial contender from 2010-2022 before hiring Napier, his destruction of the program has left a void where a once-proud national power used to be.

For another SEC powerhouse in LSU, it's a bit more complex.

If we are talking purely from an X's and O's standpoint, I believe Brian Kelly is a better coach than former Tigers head man Ed Orgeron, so I understood and even joined in the optimism for the Bayou Bengals when they hired the former to replace the latter in November 2021.

BY ADDING ED ORGERON TO STAFF, LANE KIFFIN AND LSU ADDRESS KEY FLAW FROM PREVIOUS REGIME

Coach O had won a national title while in Baton Rouge, so surely Kelly could do the same, right?

There are two main differences separating Kelly and Orgeron that made one more successful than the other: willingness to delegate and culture fit.

The culture fit piece is perhaps more nebulous but equally important, and while Orgeron fit LSU like a glove, Kelly stuck out like a sore thumb.

Kelly's inability or unwillingness to accept the "LSU way" doomed him from day one, and it's a big reason he was ousted as unceremoniously as he was while Coach O has been welcomed back with open arms.

What Orgeron lacked in game-day coaching acumen he more than made up for in recognizing talent and delegating, both on the field and with his coaches.

Having Dave Aranda and Joe Brady (along with Steve Ensminger) orchestrating the Tigers' defense and offense, respectively, led to the record-breaking 2019 season that saw quarterback Joe Burrow win a Heisman and guide LSU to a historic national championship.

Speaking of Burrow, let's transition to the other half of the equation regarding the SEC's steady decline.

Talent has started to equalize at the top, particularly between the SEC and Big Ten, and when talent is equal, coaching and quarterback play act as the tiebreaker.

We touched on coaching, but what about quarterback play?

There's no question that when the SEC was ripping off their run of national championships that the quarterbacks were outrageously talented.

Players like Tim Tebow, Cam Newton, Tua Tagovailoa, the aforementioned Burrow, and even a guy like Mac Jones were all Heisman winners or finalists who elevated the play of the team around them and ultimately captured college football's biggest prize.

Since the Big Ten started their own run of dominance in the sport, the balance of power under center has shifted heavily away from the SEC.

Even during Georgia's run of back-to-back national championships in 2021 and 2022, the Dawgs had a player like Stetson Bennett, a Heisman finalist in his own right whose stats were otherworldly despite his relative obscurity and circuitous path to becoming a starting QB.

It's not like the SEC has missed out on talented signal-callers, but it seems like all the best quarterbacks are playing for the lower-level teams in the league that have no shot at winning the title.

Hopefully for the league's sake, that changes this year with players like Arch Manning and Trinidad Chambliss leading Playoff-caliber teams near the top of the league, but it seems like whenever the league gets a quarterback that is capable of winning a championship, he ends up on either a flawed team like Jayden Daniels with LSU in 2023 or a team that just isn't talented enough like Diego Pavia on last year's Vanderbilt team.

Sometimes, transcendent quarterback play can even lift a mediocre coach to glory, as we saw with Cam Newton at Auburn in 2010.

With all due respect to Gene Chizik, he had no business winning a national championship, especially with that 2010 Auburn team, but Newton's superhero performance that season elevated them to a dream ending.

Obviously, there are way more factors that go into the shift of the balance of power in college football, and these theories are neither exhaustive nor foolproof, but they're a good start and way more in depth and nuanced than just pointing at NIL and the transfer portal.

The SEC still has the talent for a team from its ranks to win it all, and there are still plenty of great coaches and quarterbacks within the Southeastern Conference to perhaps break the drought in 2026.

Coaches like Kirby Smart, Lane Kiffin, and Steve Sarkisian have the chops to make a run this season and will have great teams with talented, veteran quarterbacks to boot.

Whether they put it all together or cede to the Big Ten once again remains to be seen, but I think I speak for everyone when I say I can't wait to see how it all plays out.

item.title: Knicks star Jalen Brunson is a man of the people, reveals the one thing he can't live without
item.description: New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson revealed video games are the one thing he can't live without, admitting he's currently hooked on FC 26 during the NBA offseason.
item.content:encoded:
New York Knicks superstar Jalen Brunson is just like so many of us: He can’t live without video games.

Brunson, 29, was asked about the one thing he couldn’t live without in an interview with his mother. His mother said family, and the two had very different answers.

"The one thing that I can’t live without is family," Sandra Brunson said in a recent interview with Lindsay Czarniak. The full interview with Brunson and his mom will premiere during the third season of Czarniak’s podcast.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"So my answer was going to be video games, but I can’t do that now," Brunson said on the show, drawing a laugh from his mother.

Brunson said he is currently playing FC 26, EA’s latest soccer game, and is waiting for the next edition of the game.

As a kid, the NBA Finals MVP was allowed to play video games on the weekend, but he had to earn his time on the console.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

"Any amount of hours he put into the video games he had to give back in the form of education whether it was reading a book so that limited (it)," Sandra said.

The former Villanova star said there was a trick, though, because he was allowed to play video games as long as he had a friend over. If his parents’ old rules still applied to Brunson, he would still be able to play a lot during the NBA season, as two of his closest friends from college, Josh Hart and Mikal Bridges, are on the Knicks.

That trio was instrumental in helping bring the Knicks their first title in 53 seasons in June.

The Knicks’ captain will look to try to follow up this year’s title with another one next summer, all while still managing to play a lot of video games.

item.title: Suspect in off-duty Philadelphia officer’s car theft linked to killing of Penn State student: police
item.description: Khadfi Fleming is wanted in a Philadelphia car theft and is also allegedly a suspect in the murder of Penn State University student Billy Schmidt.
item.content:encoded:
A man who's wanted in a recent theft of an off-duty police officer's car in Philadelphia is also a person of interest in the murder of a Penn State University student killed in June.

Billy Schmidt, 22, was killed during an armed robbery attempt that happened June 6 at about 1:30 a.m. Officers found the college student with a gunshot wound to his chest. He was taken to a hospital but pronounced dead at 1:47 a.m.

Police said 19-year-old Khadfi Fleming was allegedly involved in the theft of an off-duty police officer's car in Philadelphia.

MANHUNT UNDERWAY AFTER COLLEGE STUDENT FATALLY SHOT CHASING ROBBERS WHO ALLEGEDLY STOLE HIS PHONE

According to officials, officers in the area of 70th Street and Lindbergh Boulevard observed a red Lexus traveling without headlights, with a dark SUV following behind it. Two males were then seen running toward the Lexus before shots were fired.

Police said the suspects stole a green Dodge Charger belonging to an off-duty police officer, who pursued them and confronted them before gunfire was heard.

Officials said Fleming is also a person of interest in the murder of Schmidt.

FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

Investigators said Schmidt was on his way home after he watched the NBA Finals with his friends when he was robbed at about 1:30 a.m.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

Surveillance video appears to show Schmidt saying, "Give me my phone" as he chased the suspects. A phone could be seen thrown on the ground, then seconds later a gunshot could be heard.

Fleming's 16-year-old brother was taken into custody in Colorado in June, as was a second teenager who turned himself in to police.

Schmidt was a student at Penn State World Campus studying journalism, and was set to graduate in December.

item.title: Kaia Gerber owns 'nepo baby' status while questioning other celebrity kids: 'Show me why you deserve this job'
item.description: Kaia Gerber and Homer Gere tackle the nepo baby debate in Vogue's September cover story as they star together in Ryan Murphy's FX series "The Shards."
item.content:encoded:
Kaia Gerber and Homer Gere are confronting Hollywood’s "nepo baby" debate head-on.

In Vogue’s September 2026 cover story, Gerber, daughter of supermodel Cindy Crawford, and Gere, son of Hollywood star Richard Gere opened up about the scrutiny surrounding their careers as they step into the spotlight together in Ryan Murphy’s FX series "The Shards" and acknowledged that audiences may be quick to judge them because of their famous families.

GOLDIE HAWN SOUNDS THE ALARM ON CHILDHOOD CELEBRITY CULTURE: 'ALL I CAN SAY IS IT'S A NIGHTMARE'

"I’ve only ever been a nepo baby, and I’ve only ever benefited in my career from it," Gerber, 24, told Vogue.

The model and actress admitted she can even be skeptical of other celebrity children herself, wondering whether they have earned the opportunities they receive.

"Okay, show me why you deserve this job."

Gerber said she warned her 26-year-old co-star that audiences likely wouldn't view him the same way they would an unknown actor making his debut.

CHARLIZE THERON SAYS HER KIDS WON’T GET A FREE RIDE IN HOLLYWOOD: THEY NEED TO ‘EARN IT’

"Unfortunately with this show, it’s not like you’re just any unknown actor and people will judge you as an unknown actor," she recalled telling him, adding that the scrutiny has made her "want to work harder."

Gerber began modeling as a child and has since branched into acting, including multiple projects with Murphy.

Gere took a different route into show business.

Despite growing up with an A-list father, he said he was raised largely outside Hollywood and had never stepped onto a professional set until last year.

SHARON STONE SAYS 'EUPHORIA' SHOULD BE SHOWN IN 'EVERY HIGH SCHOOL' AND REQUIRED VIEWING FOR PARENTS

Initially, Gere brushed off suggestions that he might follow in his parents’ footsteps and studied visual arts at Brown University before becoming involved in student filmmaking.

It wasn't until a talent manager saw one of his student films, that his acting career really began. He later auditioned for both "The Shards" and HBO’s "Euphoria," landing roles in each.

Gere acknowledged that his family name inevitably complicates perceptions of his success.

"I’m a very self-critical guy who would like to believe that my career’s going well for all the wrong reasons," he told Vogue, adding that continued success has made that increasingly difficult for him to believe.

MAYA HAWKE SAYS MOM UMA THURMAN PRACTICED 'WITCH-ADJACENT' REMEDIES

The casting of Gerber and Gere carries an additional Hollywood twist.

Crawford and Richard Gere were married from 1991 to 1995 and famously appeared together on the cover of Vogue in 1992. More than three decades later, their children now share the magazine’s September cover while starring opposite each other in "The Shards."

For Gerber, however, escaping comparisons to her famous mother — and assumptions about how she landed her career — may prove impossible.

Rather than run from the "nepo baby" conversation, she appears determined to let the work make her case.

item.title: Rosie O'Donnell credits Trump for making her 're-famous' as White House calls her 'obsessed'
item.description: Rosie O'Donnell told Amy Poehler that President Trump unknowingly boosted her career, calling him "Mango Mussolini" as the White House calls her "obsessed."
item.content:encoded:
Rosie O'Donnell credited President Donald Trump for her re-discovered fame on Tuesday as the White House continued to call the actress and former co-host of "The View" "obsessed."

"I feel like recently I'm re-famous. That's what I feel. I told my kids, well kids, hold on 'cause mommy's re-famous. I don't know how it happened. I think it's Mango Mussolini," O'Donnell told "Good Hang" host Amy Poehler, referring to Trump. "I think it's him who did it. He didn't know. If he knew how much he was helping my career and my life, he would shut up about me because, you know, he's a horrible creature."

O'Donnell and the president have traded barbs over the years, as the comedian remains one of Trump's fiercest critics. She moved to Ireland after Trump's 2024 election victory over former Vice President Kamala Harris.

JIMMY KIMMEL REVEALS HE ASKED MAJOR TRUMP CRITIC TO GUEST HOST WHILE HE'S ON VACATION AS A 'SPECIAL TREAT'

The comedian has appeared on multiple podcasts and shows, and she is set to guest host Jimmy Kimmel's show for a week beginning next week.

The White House pointed Fox News Digital to one of Trump's Truth Social posts from June 6.

The post shows four images of O'Donnell with Trump appearing in thought bubbles near her head. The caption says O'Donnell "is obsessed."

O'Donnell recently claimed that she and Trump's decades-long feud has gone on in part because of their shared roots.

ROSIE O'DONNELL CLAIMS TRUMP HAS 'PTSD RESPONSE' TO HER AS BACKLASH ERUPTS

"There have been so many comedians who have said things about him, but I am from the same area that he’s from," she told Variety in July.

She and Trump were born and raised in New York, and O'Donnell said that people occasionally tell her that they sound alike, "which is probably the worst thing that you can say to me."

"But I think I’m one of those tough girls from elementary school and junior high that said to him, 'Shut the hell up! You’re not playing with us. Get out of here, you freakin’ idiot!' And he never got past it. I think I trigger him like a PTSD response of all his failures in his life as a kid."

She theorized that she reminds Trump "of the girls who said, 'You're nothing,' and it scares him."

O'Donnell made similar comments this week on Sophia Bush's "Work in Progress" podcast. When Bush said that Trump is "obsessed" with her, she agreed and said Trump "grew up with girls like me — tough, probably gay Irish girls who didn't take s--- from no stupid rich boy wannabe."

O'Donnell also signaled she would be returning to ABC's "The View" for a 30th anniversary episode in the upcoming season after detailing a tense moment with host and moderator Whoopi Goldberg.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

The show's producer, Brian Teta, posted on X that no official invites for the anniversary had gone out, appearing to refute O'Donnell.

"We love seeing all the excitement about The View’s 30th, lots of plans are in the works, but no invites have gone out," he wrote.

item.title: Vulnerable Dem's campaign pitch clashes with 'radical' voting record on top culture war issue
item.description: Sarah Trone Garriott's Iowa legislature votes on bathroom policy and girls' sports clash with her new campaign video opposing men in women's locker rooms.
item.content:encoded:
Sarah Trone Garriott, a Democratic candidate for Congress in Iowa's 3rd Congressional District, is trying to reassure voters that she doesn’t support men having access to women’s locker rooms — a stance she believes her opponents have tried to obfuscate.

"I’m a mom with two kids in Iowa public schools. Their education and safety literally keep me up at night. So, when my opponent cherry-picks and twists my record, I have to set it straight," Trone Garriott said in a recent campaign video.

"I oppose letting men in women’s locker rooms," she added.

WASHINGTON MOTHER SAYS SHE FOUND ADULT MALE SHOWERING IN WOMEN'S LOCKER ROOM DURING CHILDREN'S SWIM MEET

However, Trone Garriott's voting record from her time in the Iowa legislature is clashing with her assertions, complicating the picture for her as she attempts to flip one of the country’s most competitive House seats and topple incumbent Rep. Zach Nunn, R-Iowa.

Even before Trone Garriott captured the Democratic nomination to run in the district earlier this year, Republicans have sought to highlight parts of her record that seem to show she has championed positions farther left than the campaign she’s currently running.

Many have bashed a Muslim prayer she offered up on the Iowa Senate floor and how, as a Lutheran minister, she officiated a satanic wedding.

However, it was Trone Garriott’s stance on bathroom policy that Vice President J.D. Vance zeroed in on in a campaign speech for Nunn earlier this year.

"His opponent voted to push biological males in girls’ sports as early as kindergarten. She was voting against banning gender transition surgeries for minors," Vance said.

Vance, like other Republican critics, referred to two key votes Trone Garriott cast in the Iowa Senate: one, passed in 2023, prohibits elementary and secondary schools from letting someone enter a bathroom "that does not correspond with the person’s biological sex." A second bill, which became law in 2022, sets the eligibility rules for school and college sports teams based on biological sex.

LUTHERAN MINISTER AND HOUSE CANDIDATE UNDER FIRE AFTER RECOUNTING HER PART IN SATANIST COUPLE'S WEDDING

Trone Garriott voted against both of them.

Her votes seem consistent with previous statements she made in 2023 where she indicated bathroom policies and sports policies looking to restrict participants were based on racial and gender tensions.

"It’s very threatening of the idea of the white, male powerful figure because it muddies the waters and makes things ambiguous and confusing," Trone Garriott said in an address with the United Methodist Church, speaking on politics and faith.

"We see all sorts of responses happening in legislation and in community conflict — a lot more emphasis on really funding and supporting the private schools, the parents’ rights. And within that, the parents’ rights piece is used to enact book bans, sports bans about who can play and who can compete; it’s really couched in a language of there’s a threat to women. And white men are responsible to protect women against threats."

Her campaign did not address how her previous votes and statements align with her current campaign positions, or whether those positions have changed. But in a statement to Fox News Digital, a spokesperson for Trone Garriott said she stood by her campaign video.

"Sarah does not want men in women’s locker rooms. As a parent, there is nothing more important than the safety of our children, that’s why she will always stand up for a parent’s right to decide what’s best for their children," Zach Schenkman, the spokesperson, said.

PROGRESSIVE TALARICO KNIFES BIDEN'S OPEN BORDER, TRIES MODERATING STANCE ON KEY ISSUES IN TEXAS SENATE RACE

In her campaign video, Trone Garriott said she believed too much political attention had been given to the topic.

"Politicians have become too extreme on these issues. I’ll always put kids and families first," Trone Garriott said.

At least one Republican strategist isn't buying the switch in position.

"Even Sarah Trone Garriott's handlers realize her radical record and insane history of woke statements is completely unelectable in Iowa. No amount of false ads or consultant lies will hide the truth about the Wicked Witch of Woke and her sinister trans-for-all obsession," Zach Kraft, a spokesperson for the Republican National Committee (RNC) said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

Nunn, the district’s current representative, last won re-election in a 51.8% to 47.9% victory over Democratic challenger Lanon Baccam in 2024. With the Democratic nomination in tow, Trone Garriott will face off against Nunn in the Nov. 3 general election.

item.title: Trump administration targets Head Start bureaucracy in move advocates say puts parents in the driver's seat
item.description: President Donald Trump's proposed Head Start overhaul aims to save $2.2B and empower parents, drawing praise from Moms for Liberty while facing fierce pushback from Democrats.
item.content:encoded:
The Trump administration on Thursday announced a proposed overhaul of the federal Head Start program that would give states more control over preschool standards and could reduce administrative costs by an estimated $2.2 billion.

The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) says the proposed changes could preserve or create up to 236,000 Head Start slots. The proposal would remove several federal mandates and emphasize parents as a child’s "primary teachers." It would also establish new nutrition and physical fitness guidelines.

"Head Start began as a bold commitment to the health, dignity, and potential of every child. My uncle, Sarge Shriver, founded the program on a simple conviction: strong families, wholesome nutrition, and healthy childhood development can change the course of a child’s life," HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said in a statement.

AMERICA’S CHILD CARE CRISIS NEEDS MORE PARENTAL FREEDOM — NOT MORE WASHINGTON CONTROL

"Today, we are returning Head Start to those roots," he added. "We are removing unnecessary bureaucracy, strengthening nutrition and physical health, trusting parents and local communities, and opening Head Start to hundreds of thousands more children. That’s how we renew the promise of Head Start for the next generation." 

Head Start, established in 1965, helps low-income children prepare for school and serves them from birth to age five. It provides early education, health screenings, healthy meals and other services. The administration says the overhaul aims to reverse recent enrollment declines under the Biden administration.

The proposed changes would restructure parent committees that advise on curriculum and policy. They would also require whole, nutrient-dense foods and set daily physical activity standards. HHS says the proposal would cap administrative spending, generating an estimated $2.2 billion in savings that the department says could preserve or create up to 236,000 slots.

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS EMBRACE HEALTH AGENDA WHILE RATING RFK JR NEGATIVELY

Conservative parent advocates are praising the proposed changes, saying they would reduce federal bureaucracy and give parents more control. Moms for Liberty CEO Tina Descovich told Fox News Digital that the group supports the administration’s approach.

"We are excited to see every opportunity that parents are put in the driver's seat of their children's education and in all aspects of their life," Descovich said.

Descovich previously served on the board of a Head Start program in Brevard County, Florida. She said Moms for Liberty is "pleased" with the proposed changes and hopes they encourage parents to have "lifelong engagement in their child's education."

She added that the group supports the proposed nutrition and physical activity changes, calling Moms for Liberty members some of the "original MAHA moms in the country," referring to mothers who support the Trump administration’s "Make America Healthy Again" policies.

"We want our children eating healthy food. We support the work that Secretary Kennedy is doing in his role to clean up the food system," she said. Descovich also expressed support for Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins and said Moms for Liberty is "thrilled with what's happening to help make our children more healthy."

EXPLOSIVE REPORT FINDS $230M IN ALLEGED K-12 EDUCATION FRAUD AMID TRUMP'S CRACKDOWN: 'ESPECIALLY HIDEOUS'

Some education advocates and Democratic lawmakers argue that giving states more control over class sizes and teacher qualifications could weaken Head Start standards and lead to larger classes. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., has also criticized the proposal for removing federal health screening, math and literacy requirements.

"Trump is planning to gut Head Start — a devastating blow to our most vulnerable families," Schumer wrote in an Aug. 4 post on X. "That means no math or literacy requirements, no health & safety screenings, no guarantee children can access medical services. He doesn't give a damn. He thinks the government exists to serve only him."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

But Descovich argued that concerns about allowing states to set their own standards are "nonsense." "States have been and are in charge of education K through 12 and beyond. And there is no reason that they shouldn't be taking the Head Start program under their umbrella," she said.

item.title: MMA fighter enters with dazzling dance routine, almost immediately gets obliterated once his match begins
item.description: Ryoma Shishimoto's full K-pop dance routine to ILLIT's "It's Me" at RIZIN 54 preceded a brutal first-round TKO loss to Joe Hiramoto in Tokyo.
item.content:encoded:
The chances of me getting in the ring, octagon, or cage are slim to none, but if I did, my entrance would be solemn and dignified.

It'd be to the point that people would be wondering if they were about to watch a fight or had accidentally wandered into a funeral.

Why? Because if I entered with a K-pop dance routine and then got knocked out in the first round like one fighter in Japan just did, it would be embarrassing.

That's why.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

According to TMZ, MMA fighter Ryoma "Jolly" Shishimoto entered the ring at RIZIN 54 inside Toyota Center Tokyo by cutting a rug to South Korean girl group ILLIT's song "It's Me."

It's no "Enter Sandman," but to each their own...

But Shishimoto didn't just do a small dance. It was a full-on choreographed production.

CONOR MCGREGOR HAS SURGERY ON TORN ACL, AGAIN VOWS COMEBACK: 'MY KNEE IS REPAIRED...THANK YOU GOD'

His opponent, Joe Hiramoto, had to be licking his chops when he realized his opponent was going to be gassed from doing a dance number moments before the bell. In fact, Hiramoto dominated and ended the fight with a TKO in the first round.

Not the result you want after dancing like that. That's a routine you bust out when you've got the fight in the bag before it begins because your opponent has bronchitis or got hit by a car while walking to the arena.

Not if they're willing and able to kick your ass.

Shishimoto suffered a broken jaw and some messed-up teeth in the fight, which is a real shame.

But this might be an important lesson: don't tucker yourself out with a K-pop dance before entering the ring, and maybe don't waste time getting your choreography down pat when you could be wailing on the heavy bag.

It'd be like getting mad that you lost an arm wrestling match and said, "How did I lose?! I spent all that time learning to juggle."

Bro, you should've been curling dumbbells in your sleep.

item.title: Trump’s sly plane switch raises eyebrows over safety of passengers left behind on board
item.description: Trump secretly switched to a military jet in Turkey over an Iranian missile threat, leaving journalists and White House staff aboard the decoy aircraft.
item.content:encoded:
Reports of President Donald Trump’s secret move to a military jet during last month’s NATO summit in Turkey has put a rare security trade-off in focus: As officials apparently sought to shield Trump from a credible Iranian threat, White House staff, Secret Service agents, U.S. Military members and journalists remained aboard the decoy aircraft.

The White House did not return Fox News’ request for comment on whether officials assessed a separate risk to those left aboard the plane, which could have included Secretary of State Marco Rubio. It's not clear what, if any, protective measures were in place.

Air Force One is the call sign of the plane the U.S. president is traveling aboard, not the name of a specific aircraft.

The Washington Post first reported that Trump secretly switched to a military jet after appearing to board the older Air Force One in Turkey. Journalists and White House staff traveling with the president for the trip abroad remained on the aircraft that flew to the United Kingdom. Trump later rejoined the group before continuing home, according to the report.

TRUMP USED CATERING TRUCK, AIR FORCE ONE DECOY TO EVADE IRAN THREAT: REPORT

In a separate follow-up to that article, the Wall Street Journal reported that Israeli intelligence briefed the Trump administration on a threat to use shoulder-fired missiles against Air Force One. It also noted that Rubio was among top aides who remained aboard the older aircraft.

Former Secret Service agent Bill Gage told Fox News that the people aboard the aircraft "probably did face an elevated risk." But he described the reported operation as a calculated response to the threat environment surrounding Trump.

"Any travel with him should be considered a risk," Gage said. "I think some members of the government at the highest levels made a calculated risk to not tell anyone on the fake AF1."

The key distinction in the reporting is that the threat was allegedly aimed at the aircraft believed to be carrying Trump, rather than at the older jet itself. The secret slip-away by the president left all passengers on the plane as potential collateral of any attacks, with no public accounting of whether there were additional protections in place for them in the heightened threat environment.

Reporters traveling on the older Air Force One from Turkey to the United Kingdom recount being asked to close their window shades as the plane took off. Asked later that day whether he knew why reporters were asked to close the shades, Trump replied: "You’re probably on a dangerous flight because of the sleaze bags that we have to deal with."

"I’m number one on their list, before you," he told a reporter. "But if I go, you go right? So perhaps some day you want to change professions."

TRUMP SAYS HE'S IRAN'S 'NO. 1' TARGET AS RENEWED CONFLICT RAISES ASSASSINATION FEARS

Gage told Fox News Digital that the reported operation was likely kept to a very small circle because of the security sensitivity. "Very few people would have been told about this plan ahead of time."

He said the decision to actually move Trump to a different jet suggested officials were acting on serious intelligence.

"Overall, the threat must have been substantial and corroborated to conduct the switch/ruse. The highest levels of the government and intelligence agencies (CIA/NSA etc.) would have been involved in analyzing the threat and developing countermeasures."

Robert "Bobby" McDonald, a former senior Secret Service official, said deceptive presidential movements — sometimes referred to as "shell games" — are unusual but a part of the Secret Service playbook when credible intelligence demands extraordinary measures.

McDonald said the Air Force, rather than the Secret Service, is responsible for protecting presidential aircraft and said he believed both planes were likely being monitored.

"I find it hard to believe that those two planes were not being tracked, were not being escorted by other aircraft from either allies or our Air Force," he said. "There's no way in the world that the Secret Service, the White House staff, and the White House military office, were going to let those two planes dangle out there and and and be fending for themselves."

The Pentagon and the Air Force referred questions to the White House.

Trump's move isn't the first time Air Force One aircraft have been put to use to balk potential threats. During President Bill Clinton’s 2000 visit to Pakistan, a marked decoy aircraft arrived first and Secret Service agents disembarked before Clinton landed separately in an unmarked plane.

But the reported Turkey operation differs from many past surprise trips, in which a limited press pool traveled with the president and was sworn to secrecy.

Jake Tapper, who traveled with Obama on a secret trip to Afghanistan, said prior White Houses have used deception to protect presidents but that the reported Turkey operation was different.

"Obviously the life of the president is paramount, and previous White Houses have used deception to protect the president’s life. But no officials I’ve spoken to have ever before heard of using an AF1 full of WH staff and journalists as a decoy during an imminent threat," the CNN anchor said.

Former White House press secretary Ari Fleischer defended the reported deception as a necessary protective measure if the threat was credible.

"If the WP story about Trump switching planes to return home from Turkey is true, then kudos to the Secret Service, the Air Force and the WH," Fleischer wrote on X. "If there’s a credible threat against any POTUS, their job is to protect him. I’m sorry if the press felt deceived. In an extraordinary situation like that, what was the WH supposed to do? Announce the switch?"

item.title: Brazilian soccer player, who fell through hole in shocking viral goal celebration, gives injury update
item.description: Brazilian Jacy Maranhao revealed he was searching for his pregnant wife, and also wanted to celebrate with fans, when he fell through a stadium trap door during his celebration.
item.content:encoded:
Jacy Maranhao, the Brazilian soccer player whose goal celebration led to a horrific scene as he fell through a hole at the stadium, gave a health update on Tuesday.

Maranhao admitted he got "carried away" after scoring for his Coritiba club in Brazil at Estádio Major Antônio Couto Pereira. He said he was trying to find his wife in the crowd, which led to him jumping over the barrier on the pitch.

But a trap door was open on the other side of the barrier, which Maranhao never saw. He fell down the hole, injuring his ankle in the process.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"I scored the goal and wanted to celebrate with my wife because she’s pregnant," the 29-year-old defender and captain of Coritiba, which plays in Brazil’s top league, said, per Brazilian outlet Globo.

"But then I remembered it was my first goal at Couto Pereira stadium, and I also wanted to celebrate with the fans, but I hadn’t remembered there was a moat there."

ENGLAND'S JORDAN HENDERSON UNDERGOES SURGERY AFTER SUFFERING FRACTURE WHILE CELEBRATING WIN OVER MEXICO

Maranhao said it felt like a dream when "you’re falling from a building."

And to make matters worse, VAR review negated Maranhao’s goal, as he was ruled offsides. But Coritiba managed to win 2-1 in the end.

To everyone’s relief, though, Maranhao was able to continue playing the rest of the half despite his injury. He ended up subbing out before the game was finished.

"I twisted my foot there. It’s a bit sore, but I’m fine. Center-backs hardly ever score goals. So, when you do score…I just got carried away," Maranhao added.

The Jamaica Observer also noted Maranhao giving a quick update on social media after the viral moment hit online.

"At first it was more of a scare than anything else," he wrote, per the outlet.

"During the match my foot was quite painful and I couldn’t really put weight on it, but today I’m feeling much better and recovering well."

Maranhao played for Operário in 2024 and 2025 as well.

Maranhao is in his second season with Coritiba, which entered Série A this season after playing in Série B last year. He has scored one goal this season across 19 matches played.

item.title: Man wanted in robbery tied to Penn State student's murder now sought after off-duty cop shootout
item.description: U.S. Marshals offer a cash reward for Khadfi Fleming, 19, linked to a Penn State student's robbery case and an aggravated assault on a Philly officer.
item.content:encoded:
A 19-year-old wanted in the robbery tied to the killing of a Penn State student is now being sought in connection with another violent Philadelphia crime after an off-duty police officer exchanged gunfire with suspected car thieves.

Khadfi Fleming is a person of interest in the Monday aggravated assault of the off-duty officer, according to the U.S. Marshals Service, which is offering an immediate cash reward for information leading to his whereabouts.

The confrontation unfolded early Monday after thieves allegedly targeted the officer's Dodge Charger, Fox 29 Philadelphia reported.

OFF-DUTY TROOPER AND ARMED CITIZEN HAILED AS HEROES AFTER RETURNING FIRE ON IN-N-OUT GUNMAN

The off-duty officer followed the suspects and confronted them, leading to an exchange of gunfire, according to the outlet. No one is believed to have been struck.

The suspects escaped, and investigators later recovered the officer's Charger with a broken window and damage to its steering column, along with numerous 9mm shell casings, Fox 29 reported.

Authorities say the suspects moved to another stolen car – a Lexus that was later found abandoned.

The U.S. Marshals Service has since publicly identified Fleming as a person of interest in the aggravated assault.

MARSHALS NAB TEEN WANTED FOR MURDER OF PENN STATE STUDENT 1,700 MILES FROM CRIME SCENE, 2ND SUSPECT IN CUSTODY

"USMS Philly is offering an immediate cash reward for Khadfi Fleming, 19, wanted for robbery," the agency wrote on X, adding that Fleming is also a "person of interest" in the Monday attack on the off-duty officer.

Fleming has not been charged in connection with the Monday incident.

But authorities were already looking for the 19-year-old before the latest violence.

Fleming is wanted on a robbery charge connected to the June killing of Billy Schmidt, a 22-year-old Penn State student who was shot while walking home from an NBA Finals watch party.

MANHUNT UNDERWAY AFTER COLLEGE STUDENT FATALLY SHOT CHASING ROBBERS WHO ALLEGEDLY STOLE HIS PHONE

Schmidt was just blocks from his South Philadelphia home when he was fatally shot around 1:30 a.m. on June 6.

Surveillance video captured the final moments before the shooting, with Schmidt heard asking for his stolen phone back before a gunshot rang out.

His father, Bill Schmidt, previously described his son as someone who "cared about everybody and never hurt or bothered a soul."

MANHUNT UNDERWAY FOR KANSAS CITY SHOOTING SPREE SUSPECT NEAR WORLD CUP VENUE; FBI OFFERING $25K REWARD

"For him to get shot like that is a travesty," he told ABC7.

The killing sparked a search for two 16-year-old murder suspects, including Fleming's younger brother.

U.S. Marshals captured Azzubair Outen-Fleming in Colorado Springs, Colorado, about a month after Schmidt's death. Authorities said the teenager was found at a distant relative's home and initially tried to conceal his identity.

Philadelphia Police Department Deputy Commissioner Frank Vanore said Outen-Fleming would face a murder charge, Fox 29 reported.

NEW YORK STATE POLICE LAUNCH MANHUNT AFTER KILLING, HOUSE FIRE FOR 'ARMED AND DANGEROUS' SUSPECT

The second teen, Kaiseem Smith, surrendered to Philadelphia police.

Schmidt was studying digital journalism and media at Penn State and was expected to graduate in December.

Now, two months after his killing, authorities are seeking the elder Fleming as they investigate whether he was involved in the latest violent encounter.

Anyone with information about Fleming's whereabouts is urged to contact the U.S. Marshals Service at 1-866-865-TIPS (8477).

Fox News Digital has reached out to the Philadelphia Police Department and U.S. Marshals Service for additional information and comment.

Fox News Digital's Louis Casiano and Adam Sabes contributed to this report.

item.title: Golfer Hailey Ostrom is Team Sophie, Hilary Duff compares herself to LeBron & pig squealing contests!
item.description: Hilary Duff's viral LeBron James moment on her Lucky Me Tour, Sophie Cunningham's new golf ally, and France's pig-squealing contest are here.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com.

Over the weekend, I had a conversation with a bartender whose boyfriend just got deployed.

"All I do is work and gym and sit around the apartment feeling sorry for myself because he's not here. I need a hobby," she said. "What do you do for fun?"

I told her maybe I'm not the right person to ask. Because all I do it work and gym as well. Throw in a Saturday trek through the woods here and there.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK

And the hobbies I do have maybe aren't very exciting for a bartender in her early 20s. I'm in a book club, and I've recently become fixated on houseplants. I fear I'm just a couple of knitting needles away from the geriatric trifecta. And in my 30s, no less!

But then what do I run across this morning? A video of Wiz Khalifa absolutely giddy over his houseplants:

I mean, I knew he was pretty fond of at least one particular type of plant (the kind you're not allowed to grow in your house), but I was not expecting Bird of Paradise and Monstera.

So maybe I'm not so uncool after all. Or all of us Millennials are just following the exact same pipeline.

Speaking of, today we're checking in on Millennial Queen Hilary Duff, who is comparing herself to an NBA star. Plus, we've found another Sophie Cunningham ally (certainly not in the WNBA, though), and there's some weird stuff going on in France.

Like, really weird.

Pour yourself a cocktail, drop your work phone into a houseplant, and let's get rolling.

Hilary Duff feels just like LeBron James

I recruited that bartender to my book club, by the way. So there's a win.

Anyway, Hilary Duff went viral during a show on her Lucky Me Tour in Philadelphia Sunday night.

"We started in Florida, went to LA, we've ended up here," she said. "I'm starting to feel like LeBron!"

She had that one in the holster with the safety off. Could not wait to deploy it.

It was cute, though, I laughed. And besides, I'll tolerate no Hilary Duff slander in this column.

I will, however, tolerate LeBron James slander. Actually, as a Pacers fan who had to suffer through his "Big 3" Miami Heat era, I encourage LeBron slander.

Get a load of his agent, Rich Paul, blabbering on about how athletes have "the hardest job in the world."

The hardest job in the world.

Now, look, I get it. Athletes have a physically demanding job, and there's a lot of pressure on them.

There's also a lot of pressure on police officers, brain surgeons, air traffic controllers, school bus drivers... need me to go on?

But this dude (whose name is literally "Rich") thinks that the hardest job in the world is… getting paid millions of dollars to play sports. Just because their family and friends ask them for money. And because $100 million is "really $50 million after taxes."

Let me find my tiny violin.

It reminds me of a time when I worked for the Titans as a social media manager, and the team was going through a particularly tough camp workout. A high-profile player — whom I won't name — said to me on the sideline, "Can we trade jobs? You go do this and I just play with my phone?"

I said, "We trading salaries, too?"

Wide-eyed, he said, "NOPE!" then ran right back onto the field.

That's what I thought.

Hailey Ostrom shows her support for Sophie Cunningham

Sadly, I don't think I'd make it in the NFL. I wouldn't make it in the WNBA, either. The Lord has given me many blessings in life, but height isn't one of them. And I'm pretty sure the last time I played basketball was sometime around the fourth grade, so I'm probably a little rusty.

Look, I am so sick of talking about the WNBA. And I'd say you guys are probably sick of reading about it — but clearly you're not. I see those analytics. WNBA soap opera stories are CLICKERS.

Particularly the ones involving Sophie Cunningham.

And while (seemingly) the entire league is ganging up on Sophie, a new ally has emerged. Golfer Hailey Ostrom has entered the chat.

I am no expert on the hierarchy of golf influencers. You'd have to talk to my colleague Joe Kinsey about that. I am, however, comfortable saying Hailey is in the top 3. I think Paulina Gretzky is in there, too. But I don't think either have dethroned Paige Spiranac.

PAULINA GRETZKY HIT THE GOLF COURSE DRESSED FOR SUCCESS AND WON, BROOKS NADER IN HER BAYWATCH RED & A SQUIRREL

Maybe one day.

Maybe when the WNBA assembles its task force to determine what a woman is, the commish can call in Hailey to testify. Or literally any human being with a brain — which seems to be extra hard to find in that league lately.

Who's signing up for France's annual pig-squealing championship?

Yes, friends, that is a thing. For 43 years running!

Which means that while France was wrestling with inflation, unemployment and political upheaval in the early 1980s, one visionary looked at the state of the nation and thought, "Enough of this. We need to know who does the best pig impression."

A dignified, time-honored and storied tradition was born.

Just look at those patriots making their country proud.

The 2026 installment of this contest took place over the weekend, and a fella named Noel Jamet won — claiming his 10th title. A record!

Some say he's the GOAT of pig squealing. An athlete on par with Michael Jordan, Tom Brady and Serena Williams.

But we'll never know until he takes on the true champion. And my fellow "South Park" fans know exactly who that is.

Let's open the mailbag.

🐦 Twitter/X: @TheAmberHarding

📸 Instagram: @amberharding

Caitlyn W. writes: I remember reading in Nightcaps that you were planning to do the HYROX race in Nashville, and I'm convinced you have to know someone to get into one of these things.

Last time I tried, I made an account ahead of time, set a reminder for when registration opened, and was on the website right when tickets went on sale. I even had my husband trying on his laptop at the same time. We both sat in the queue forever, and by the time either of us got through, sold out. I mean WTF.

Amber:

Sounds like me buying Garth Brooks tickets a few weeks ago.

But yeah, I've kind of given up on HYROX for that exact reason. There are plenty of ways to torture myself that don't involve a waitlist.

I actually signed up for a Spartan Super race in October. I've never done one before, so pray for me. I'm not worried about the running part... or the mud or even leaping over fire. It's all the obstacles that I can't practice in my regular gym that I'm worried about.

That and the superhuman grip strength I'm told you have to possess to finish one of these things.

There's a Ninja Warrior gym here in Middle Tennessee. I'm probably going to go there to train at least a few times. Which sounds ridiculous, but I'm committed to not humiliating myself on race day.

But hey, at least I don't have to wear 125 T-shirts.

Remember when I told y'all there's a Guinness World Record for literally everything? There truly is.

Anyway, if anyone has any Spartan training tips, send them my way.
